description: Validates the schema.json file for an account definition. Use secretSchema for secret credential fields, optionsSchema for non-secret option fields. Both can coexist if needed.

secretSchema.description: Validates secret credential fields stored encrypted (e.g. accessToken, apiKey).

properties.description: Each key is a secret field name. Pattern for required fields: '(^\{\{.*\|\|(.*)\}\}$)|^(.{1,500})$' (min length 1). Pattern for non-required fields: '(^\{\{.*\|\|(.*)\}\}$)|^(.{0,200})$' (min length 0).

optionsSchema.description: Validates non-secret option fields (e.g. environment, region). Can be present alongside secretSchema when there are non-secret option fields.

properties.description: Each key is an option field name. Can be empty {} for OAuth accounts with no option fields.

combinedSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema (draft-07) that validates the nested document { options, secret } as a single unit, for cross-field rules an independent optionsSchema/secretSchema cannot express (e.g. Snowflake authenticationType -> which secret is required). It supplements those schemas rather than replacing them: config-backend runs it in place of the two on the account create/edit path, but optionsSchema/secretSchema stay the field contract for every other consumer -- notably the OAuth path, which validates against optionsSchema alone and never sees a combinedSchema. That is why the anyOf below still requires one of them: a definition carrying only a combinedSchema would leave those consumers validating against nothing. Loosely typed here because it may use if/then/else, const, etc.
